chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if you disclose your charitable expenditures, it is good; and if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is besides the Zakat. Indeed, the giving of Zakat is public, not secret.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between concealed charity and Zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'better' form of charity in the verse refers to voluntary *sadaqah* given in secret, distinguishing it from obligatory *Zakat*, which is generally public. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the different spiritual merits and social functions of obligatory versus voluntary giving, reinforcing the value of humility in private charity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:271] If you give alms openly, it is good, and if you hide it and give it to the poor, it is better for you.
So heasws said: ‘It is besides the Zakāt. The (giving) of Zakāt is publicly, without being secretive’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘. . . If you pay it privately to the needy, it is better for you. . . .’ [2:273],
has said, ‘This payment is a payment other than compulsory zakat which is paid publicly and not privately.’”
